## Seneca on life

Seneca (c. 4 BCE–65 CE) approaches life within Stoicism. Philosophy is therapy for destructive passions; anger especially must be starved before it hardens into cruelty. Time is our scarcest good; busyness without reflection wastes life. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets life most directly—useful for searches such as “seneca quotes on life.”
